article.Citation/Title: Jensen, M. E., Stenbaek, D. S., Fisher, P. M., Knudsen, G. M., & Fink-Jensen, A. (2024). Single-dose psilocybin therapy for alcohol use disorder: Pharmacokinetics, feasibility, safety, and efficacy in an open-label study. Research Square preprint.
article.InterventionDescription: Single 25 mg oral psilocybin dose (PEX010 capsule) within a 5-session open-label therapy course (2 preparation, 1 dosing, 2 integration sessions) delivered by trained therapists at a Copenhagen research clinic.

ae_events.Description: Anxiety, one of the most frequently reported of 46 adverse events, occurring within the first 24 hours of dosing.
Headache, one of the most frequently reported of 46 adverse events, occurring within the first 24 hours of dosing.

article.Citation/Title: This is a Research Square preprint (posted August 23, 2024, DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-4947184/v1), not peer reviewed at the time of the version extracted; the article's own header states 'Preprints are preliminary reports that have not undergone peer review.' Coded exactly what the preprint reports, per instruction, with preprint status flagged here rather than altering the citation string.
article.Outcome: No single sentence in Methods designates one named 'primary outcome,' but the Abstract's Results paragraph leads with the SUD-behavioral finding ('Alcohol consumption significantly decreased... Heavy drinking days were reduced by 37.5 percentage points'), and the Results section 'Clinical outcomes' reports this identical contrast with an author-computed standardized effect size: 'The percentage of heavy drinking days decreased from baseline to week 12 by -37.5% (95% CI, -61.1, -13.9, p = .005, Cohen's d = 1.02).' Per field precedence (SUD-behavioral outcome the abstract leads with) and the instruction to prefer a numeric effect size, used the author-reported Cohen's d = 1.02 for this baseline-to-week-12 contrast rather than the raw -37.5 percentage-point mean difference, since Cohen's d is directly stated in the same sentence and is the field's preferred numeric form.
article.SD: No separate t/F/chi-squared statistic is reported for this contrast (the linear mixed model's effect size is reported directly as Cohen's d, not as a t-statistic). The only paired dispersion measure given in the same sentence is the 95% CI on the raw mean difference (-61.1, -13.9 percentage points); reported this CI and flagged that it is on the raw-difference scale, not a standard error on the d value itself, since no SE/CI for d was separately reported.
article.PVal: p = .005, same sentence as Outcome/SD (Results, 'Clinical outcomes').
article.SampleSize_NFinal: All ten enrolled participants completed the psilocybin therapy course (Results, 'Feasibility...': 'All ten participants completed the psilocybin therapy course'). Methods, 'Statistical analysis' states missing clinical-outcome data (due to relapse) were imputed via worst-observed-value carried forward rather than excluded, so the week-12 linear-mixed-model analysis retained all n=10; Results also references 'the 10 participants' as the denominator for individual-level response counts at week 4/week 12.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 13 of 14 elements are explicitly described. Comparator, randomization and blinding are each described as absent ('open-label, single-group' design stated in Methods; Discussion names 'lack of a control group... and an open-label design' as a limitation), satisfying the described-including-as-absent rule. Setting is detailed (Copenhagen University Clinic for Psychedelic Research, recruitment, session structure). sample_size_power is the sole unmet criterion: no a priori power calculation or formal sample-size justification is reported anywhere; the only sample-size-related comment is a Discussion aside that the study could not assess a sex effect 'due to sample size limitations,' which addresses a secondary/exploratory subgroup question rather than describing how the overall sample size or power for the primary analysis was determined, so it was judged insufficient to satisfy this specific criterion.

article.RandomizationYN: Investigator-initiated 'open-label, single-group' design (Methods, 'Study design and overview'); no randomization was performed or discussed as absent-by-design. Per the v1.2 single-arm boundary rule, coded 0 (absent), not 3.
article.BlindingYN: Open-label study; Discussion explicitly lists 'an open-label design' among key limitations. Coded 0 per the single-arm boundary rule, not 3.
article.Double+Blind: Consistent with BlindingYN = 0; the study is open-label throughout, not double-blind.
article.Comparator: No control or comparison arm; Discussion states 'lack of a control group' as a key limitation. Only one fixed dose (25 mg) was administered to all participants, so there is no high-vs-low dose comparator design either. Coded 0, not 3, per the single-arm boundary rule.
article.PrimaryCare: No mention of primary-care settings or providers; all sessions took place at the Copenhagen University Clinic for Psychedelic Research, a specialised psychiatric research clinic. The concept is not inapplicable to a clinical AUD trial in general, so coded 0 (absent) rather than 3.
article.Power: No a priori or post hoc power calculation is reported for the study's primary analyses anywhere in Methods, Results, or Discussion. The Discussion's 'Due to sample size limitations, we were unable to ascertain if sex influenced the effects of psilocybin' pertains specifically to an exploratory sex-subgroup question, not a general statement that the primary analysis was underpowered, so it was judged not to meet the 'bare statement of underpowered' bar for this field. Coded 0; flagged as a borderline call given the Discussion's sample-size comment.
article.Retention (%): Study is not randomized, so denominator is the enrolled sample. Participants section: 10 were 'ultimately included' (enrolled); Results, 'Feasibility...': 'All ten participants completed the psilocybin therapy course.' Retention = 10/10 x 100 = 100.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1 on both statistical-adjustment and substantive-discussion grounds: the linear mixed model explored whether Cmax, AUCPPC, AUCSDI and MEQ30 score were associated with the clinical outcome as covariates (Statistical analysis), Spearman correlations tested baseline factors (age, weight, BMI, liver/kidney function) against PK/PD parameters (Table S4), and the Discussion explicitly names candidate confounds not otherwise controlled: 'selection bias due to self-referral and high expectations from positive widespread media coverage may have influenced, at least in part, the observed positive effects.'
article.BaseStatus: Results, 'Participant demographics': 'Participants met 8 (7-10) of the AUD criteria, indicating severe AUD (defined as >= 6 symptoms out of 11), supported by an AUDIT score of 23.5 (20.2-27).' Author-assigned severity label used directly.
article.Age_Median: Median age 44 years (41-49) (Abstract; Participants section) falls within the 30-50 bracket.
article.PercentFem: Abstract and Participants: 'ten treatment-seeking adults (eight men and two women...)'. 2/10 = 20%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: No race or ethnicity data appear in the provided main text; the article refers detailed participant characteristics to 'Table S1 in the supplementary,' which is not part of the converted text supplied for extraction. Coded '.' rather than fabricating or inferring from the Danish recruitment setting.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: No income, employment, insurance status, or low-income eligibility criterion is reported anywhere in the article. Coded 0.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: All procedures, recruitment (via www.alkoholforskning.dk/psilocybin, 'all regions of Denmark'), ethics approval (Danish Ethics Committee of the Capital Region, Copenhagen) and clinical site (Copenhagen University Clinic for Psychedelic Research) are in Denmark. Emitted 'NonUS' per the closed-enum rule; actual country (Denmark) recorded here.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0. Participants section funnel: 37 individuals expressed interest, 15 underwent screening, 10 were included (a narrowly screened, self-referred, treatment-seeking volunteer sample recruited via a dedicated study website). Discussion explicitly names 'selection bias due to self-referral and high expectations from positive widespread media coverage' as a limitation affecting generalisability.
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: Coded 1: blood pressure and heart rate were repeatedly measured as a study outcome (Methods, 'Feasibility, cardiovascular effects, and adverse effects': 'Blood pressure and heart rate were repeatedly measured in parallel with plasma psilocin concentrations'; Results reports psilocybin 'moderately increased systolic blood pressure' with reference to Figure S2), and plasma psilocin concentration is itself a biomarker outcome reported as a primary pharmacokinetic endpoint (Table 1).
article.Followup in months: This is a single-dose intervention (Day 0 dosing, with integration sessions at +1 and +7 days only), so there is no meaningfully separate 'end of treatment' horizon distinct from the from-baseline (Day 0) follow-up clock; all outcome time points (week 1, week 4, week 12) are measured from the dosing day. Longest reported clinical follow-up is week 12 (Table 2; Abstract: 'Alcohol consumption significantly decreased over the 12 weeks'). Converted 12 weeks / 4 weeks-per-month = 3, consistent with the codebook's 2-weeks-=-0.5 convention.
article.CessationMeasured: Coded 0. Unlike studies reporting a discrete abstinence/cessation rate, this article reports only continuous/percentage measures -- percentage of heavy drinking days, percentage of drinking days, and drinks per day (Table 2) -- with no distinct binary or rate-based 'cessation' or 'abstinence' outcome named anywhere in the text.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 0. The word 'relapse' appears only once, incidentally, in the missing-data-handling description ('Missing data in the clinical outcomes were due to relapse and were consequently replaced with the participants' worst value observed'; Statistical analysis). This is not presented as a formally tracked or reported relapse outcome with its own metric, so RelapseMeasured is coded 0; flagged as a borderline call given the explicit mention of relapse as a cause of missingness.
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 1: feasibility is an explicitly named study aim and outcome (Abstract, 'Aims'; Results, 'Feasibility, cardiovascular effects, and adverse effects': 'The feasibility... [was] determined by the proportion of participants who completed all sessions of the psilocybin therapy'), and Results reports 100% completion as the feasibility finding.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Results, 'Feasibility...': 'A total of 46 adverse events were recorded, all categorised as mild, transient, and self-limiting... The most frequent adverse events were anxiety, headache, and fatigue.' Only these three named types are identifiable from the provided text; the full per-type breakdown is in Table S2, which is referenced but not included in the converted text supplied for this extraction. Because 'most frequent' implies additional, less-common AE types exist among the 46 total events that cannot be named from the available text, coded 'Not numbered' rather than fabricating a count of 3.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: The article reports a total event count (46) and names the three most frequent types but never states how many distinct participants experienced >=1 AE (overlap across types/participants is not addressed and Table S2, which likely contains this, is not in the provided text). Coded '.' rather than inferring an unsupported total.
article.AE_denominator: All ten participants received the psilocybin dosing session and were monitored under the same feasibility/safety assessment (Results: 'All ten participants completed the psilocybin therapy course'; AEs assessed as part of this same monitoring). AE_denominator = 10.

ae_events.Jensen 2024_AE01: Severity 'Mild' is author-assigned, not rubric-derived: the article states all 46 recorded AEs were 'categorised as mild, transient, and self-limiting, without requiring intervention,' and separately that 'No participants required rescue medication during the study period,' which directly supports InterventionRequired = 'N' and MeetsFDASerious = 'N' for this type. No per-type participant count (NAffected) is given for anxiety specifically -- only that it was among the three most frequent of 46 total events -- so NAffected = '.'. Onset coded 'post-session-acute' per the article's statement that the most frequent AEs 'occurred within the first 24 hours of dosing.' Considered whether this should be coded AE_type = 'challenging_experience' given anxiety's overlap with expected in-session phenomenology described in the Dosing session narrative, but the authors report this anxiety within their own formal 46-event AE tally (distinct from the separate subjective-drug-intensity/quality-of-experience assessments), so it was coded as a clinical 'AE' following the article's own classification.
ae_events.Jensen 2024_AE02: Same author-assigned Mild severity and same 24-hour post-dosing onset window as AE01, drawn from the identical sentence in Results, 'Feasibility...'. NAffected = '.' because no per-type count is given, only that headache was among the three most frequent of 46 total AEs.
ae_events.Jensen 2024_AE03: Same author-assigned Mild severity and same 24-hour post-dosing onset window as AE01/AE02, drawn from the identical sentence in Results, 'Feasibility...'. NAffected = '.' because no per-type count is given, only that fatigue was among the three most frequent of 46 total AEs.

config_proposal.note: Author-reported Cohen's d = 1.02 (baseline to week 12, percentage heavy drinking days, the primary SUD-behavioral contrast this study's Results and Abstract lead with), explicitly stated as 'corrected for correlation between the repeated measurements' (Methods, 'Statistical analysis'). Although the value is directly reported rather than derived, it is a within-subjects pre/post effect size from a single-arm design being fed into a between-groups Tier-1 forest-plot pipeline -- the same structural approximation flagged in this corpus's other single-arm psilocybin-AUD studies -- so confidence is set to 'approx' rather than 'clean', consistent with the instruction to prefer 'approx' when in doubt.
